caption:
Google's $5 AI Plus plan loses access to Gemini's Pro models on November 13.
Picking Pro in the Gemini app or AI Mode will need Google AI Pro, which costs $20 a month.
AI Plus keeps the faster Flash models, and old Pro chats can continue with another model.

Would you pay 4 times more to keep Gemini Pro?

paragraphs.text: Google AI Plus subscribers will lose the ability to choose Gemini's Pro models on November 13, 2026, according to reports from 9to5Google and Android Central. The change covers both the Gemini app and AI Mode in Google Search. After that date, Pro models will be limited to people who pay for Google AI Pro or a higher plan.

Google started telling subscribers about the change in mid-October in an email from the Google One team. 9to5Google reported on October 14 that a Reddit user had shared the message and that several other subscribers said they had received it too. Android Central said Droid-Life also reported on the email.

According to the email cited by 9to5Google, Pro models will only be offered to Google AI Pro subscribers and above. Conversations that AI Plus members started with a Pro model are not deleted. The email says those chats can be continued with a different model instead.

AI Plus subscribers keep access to Google's Flash and Flash-Lite models 9to5Google reported. Android Central likewise said users on the plan can keep using Flash models in the Gemini app and in AI Mode. Google's free tier, which includes Flash-Lite, stays in place.
The price gap between the plans

In the United States, Google AI Plus costs $5 a month, while Google AI Pro costs $20 a month, Android Central reported. That makes continued Pro access four times as expensive for anyone who upgrades. The outlet listed other AI Pro benefits, including 5TB of cloud storage shared across Google services, YouTube Premium Lite, Google Home Premium and Google Health Premium, along with Google's latest Gemini models.

The cut follows an earlier change to Google's subscription lineup announced in October, 9to5Google reported. It also came shortly before the launch of Gemini 4 Argon, a model Google made available to AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers rather than to AI Plus members.
Neither report quotes a public statement from Google beyond the email sent to subscribers and the help center article it points to.

For people who joined AI Plus mainly to reach Gemini's strongest models, the plan now offers less than it did when they signed up. The change draws a sharper line between Google's paid tiers: the cheapest plan covers the fast Flash models for everyday use, and the most capable models sit behind the $20 plan. It also gives Google a clearer reason to move budget subscribers up a tier.

AI Plus subscribers who rely on Pro models have until November 13, 2026 to decide whether to upgrade to Google AI Pro or stay on Flash models. The next thing to watch is whether Google changes the AI Plus price or adds new benefits to keep budget subscribers on the plan.
